articles.title: High Court decision means landlord licensing will go ahead
articles.summary: The High Court has for the second time  dismissed a judicial review of Thurrock council’s Selective Licensing Scheme. The claimant had sought an oral hearing to challenge the High Court’s previous written decision to dismiss the claim on March 13 this year.  That decision allowed the authority to start to implement the scheme. The court has […]
articles.ai_summary:
- The High Court has upheld Thurrock council's Selective Licensing Scheme by dismissing a judicial review, paving the way for its implementation.
- This marks the second rejection of the claimant's challenge, reaffirming the council's authority to regulate landlord licensing.

articles.summary: Tenants are increasingly discerning, claims the agent
articles.ai_summary:

Erewash council launched its prosecution of landlord Mahmood Rahemtulla after he ignored a request to supply documentation about tenancy agreements and rent deposits at the five-bed house in Long Eaton. The council also […]
articles.ai_summary:
- Landlord Mahmood Rahemtulla fined £1,145 after Erewash Council's court action for failing to provide tenancy and rent documentation for his HMO.
- The legal action underscores ongoing scrutiny of rental compliance, despite the relatively small financial penalty imposed.
